name: OPA340NA_3K
title: OPA340, OPA2340, OPA4340: single-supply rail-to-rail CMOS op amps, 5.5 MHz
summary: A family of CMOS operational amplifiers for single supplies from 2.5 V to 5.5 V: OPA340 holds one amplifier, OPA2340 two and OPA4340 four, each built independently and specified alike. Inputs reach past both rails and the class AB output comes within a few millivolts of either rail with light loads. Each amplifier gives 5.5 MHz of gain bandwidth and 6 V/µs on 750 µA, is unity-gain stable, and suits driving sampling A/D converters, audio and active filters. OPA2340UA is the dual in the 8-pin SOIC, sold in tubes of 75.
key_figures: 2.7 V to 5 V specified, 2.5 V to 5.5 V operating; 5.5 V absolute maximum
1 mV typ, 5 mV max at RL = 100 kΩ

circuits.title: Input current protection for voltages beyond the supply
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower fed through 5 kΩ at its non-inverting input. When the input signal goes more than 500 mV outside a supply rail, the clamp diodes conduct and the resistor holds the overload current to 10 mA or less.

parts.note: limits input overload current to 10 mA max

circuits.title: Series output resistor for capacitive load drive at unity gain
circuits.description: A unity-gain follower whose feedback comes straight from the amplifier output, with RS of 10 Ω to 20 Ω between that output and a load of RL in parallel with CL. RS damps the ringing a big load capacitance would cause. RS and RL form a divider, so the output carries a small DC error and loses a little swing: about 0.2% with RL = 10 kΩ and RS = 20 Ω.

circuits.title: Noninverting buffer driving the ADS7816 12-bit A/D converter
circuits.description: OPA340 as a unity-gain follower on a single 5 V supply drives the ADS7816 through a 500 Ω and 3300 pF low-pass network that filters high-frequency noise. An input of 0 V to 5 V gives 0 V to 5 V at the converter, whose input range is 0 to VREF. The converter's supply and reference pins both take 5 V, each with a 0.1 µF capacitor to ground; its serial clock, data and chip-select lines go to the host.
notes: ADS7816 pins: VREF 1, +IN 2, -IN 3, GND 4, CS/SHDN 5, DOUT 6, DCLOCK 7, V+ 8.

circuits.title: Inverting amplifier driving the ADS7816 12-bit A/D converter
circuits.description: OPA340 as an inverting amplifier of gain -1 (5 kΩ in, 5 kΩ feedback) with 330 pF across the feedback resistor to roll off high frequencies, driving the ADS7816 directly. An input of 0 V to -5 V gives 0 V to 5 V at the converter. The non-inverting input sits at ground; the converter's supply and reference both take 5 V with 0.1 µF each to ground.
notes: ADS7816 pins: VREF 1, +IN 2, -IN 3, GND 4, CS/SHDN 5, DOUT 6, DCLOCK 7, V+ 8.

circuits.title: Speech bandpass filter, 160 Hz to 2.4 kHz
circuits.description: Both halves of an OPA2340 on a single 5 V supply. The input is AC-coupled by 200 pF into a mid-supply bias made of two 10 MΩ resistors, which with the coupling capacitor sets the low corner; amplifier A buffers that node as a follower. Amplifier B is a unity-gain Sallen-Key low-pass stage (243 kΩ and 1.74 MΩ in series, 47 pF to ground at the non-inverting input, 220 pF from the junction of the resistors to the output) that sets the upper corner. The output drives RL to ground.

circuits.title: Noninverting amplifier with a single-pole low-pass input filter
circuits.description: R1 and C1 form a low-pass filter at the non-inverting input; RF and RG set a noninverting gain of 1 + RF/RG, 10 V/V (20 dB) with the values given. C1 = 10 nF puts the corner at 15.9 kHz and C1 = 1 µF at 159 Hz; with no C1 the bandwidth is the amplifier's gain bandwidth divided by the closed-loop gain.

circuits.title: Two-pole Sallen-Key low-pass filter with gain
circuits.description: R2, R1, C1 and C2 make a second-order Sallen-Key low-pass filter in front of a noninverting gain of (RG + RF)/RG = 10. C2 runs from the junction of R2 and R1 back to the output. R2 = 10 × R1 and C2 = C1/10 keep the two RC sections from loading each other. With C1 = 10 nF and C2 = 1 nF the corner is 15.9 kHz; C1 = 1 µF and C2 = 0.1 µF move it to 159 Hz. The amplifier's effective bandwidth should be at least ten times the cutoff, or phase shift in the amplifier makes the corner less precise.

operation.text: OPA340 is the single, OPA2340 the dual and OPA4340 the quad. The amplifiers in a dual or quad share nothing but the supply pins, which keeps crosstalk low, and all three carry the same specifications. OPA340 comes in 5-pin SOT-23, 8-pin SOIC and 8-pin PDIP; OPA2340 in 8-pin VSSOP, SOIC and PDIP; OPA4340 in 16-pin SSOP and 14-pin SOIC. An enhanced-product version, OPA340-EP, is listed for defence, aerospace and medical use.
The amplifiers are made on a 0.6 µm CMOS process and are stable at unity gain. The class AB output can drive 600 Ω loads.

Full specification covers 2.7 V to 5 V and the part runs from 2.5 V to 5.5 V; the specified parameters hold across the whole specified supply range, and many apply from -40°C to 85°C. Parameters that move noticeably with supply or temperature are in the typical-characteristics graphs. There is one operating mode, entered once the supply exceeds 2.7 V (±1.35 V); the supply maximum is 5.5 V (±2.75 V). A supply above 7 V can destroy the part.

Two input pairs work in parallel: an N-channel pair handles inputs from about (V+) - 1.3 V up to 500 mV above V+, and a P-channel pair handles inputs from 500 mV below V- up to about (V+) - 1.3 V. Both are on in a band typically from (V+) - 1.5 V to (V+) - 1.1 V. That 400 mV band moves by ±300 mV from part to part, so it may lie anywhere from (V+) - 1.8 V to (V+) - 1.4 V at the low extreme up to (V+) - 1.2 V to (V+) - 0.8 V at the high one. Laser trimming matches the offset of the two pairs for good CMRR and a smooth handover, but inside the band PSRR, CMRR, offset, offset drift and THD can be worse than elsewhere. A double-folded cascode combines the two pairs and feeds the class AB output stage.

Input bias current is normally about 200 fA. Driving an input more than 500 mV past either supply makes large current flow through the input clamps. Brief excursions of that size are survivable if the input current stays at or below 10 mA, which a series input resistor such as 5 kΩ ensures; a source that cannot deliver 10 mA needs no resistor.

The class AB output stage uses common-source transistors. With light loads above 50 kΩ the output typically comes within a few millivolts of each rail; with loads from 2 kΩ to 50 kΩ it stays tens of millivolts from each rail while keeping high open-loop gain. Driven as a unity-gain follower on 5 V with 10 kΩ to V/2, a 5 VPP sine input gives about 4.98 VPP at the output.

Load capacitance and the amplifier's output resistance (plus any load resistance) add a pole that erodes phase margin, and the unity-gain connection is the most sensitive to it. At unity gain the amplifiers handle a purely capacitive load up to about 1000 pF; higher closed-loop gain allows more capacitance. At unity gain, putting 10 Ω to 20 Ω between the output pin and the load greatly reduces ringing when the load capacitance is large, at the price of a small DC divider error with any resistive load (about 0.2% for RL = 10 kΩ and RS = 20 Ω) and slightly less swing.

The amplifiers are aimed at sampling converters running at up to 100 kHz, and also work with faster ones. They buffer the converter's input capacitance and the charge kicked back at each sample while also providing gain. Noise filtering at high frequencies comes from a series-R, shunt-C network after a noninverting stage, or from a capacitor in parallel with the feedback resistor of an inverting stage.

The supply pins need bypassing with 0.01 µF ceramic capacitors. A 0.1 µF bypass capacitor placed close to the supply pins keeps noise and impedance of the supply from coupling errors into the amplifier.

Keep traces short, use a ground plane and place surface-mount parts as close to the pins as possible, with a 0.1 µF capacitor right across the supply pins; these measures also lower susceptibility to electromagnetic interference. Route input traces as far from supply lines as possible, keep RF and RG close to the part and to each other to cut parasitics, and use low-ESR ceramic bypass capacitors. The OPA340 is designed for low sensitivity to radio-frequency interference, which shows up as a shift in offset or DC level, though an intense RF field may yet shift the offset.
Built-in ESD protection is limited. Store and handle the parts with their leads shorted together or in conductive foam to protect the MOS gates.
